scope: Retrospective local Kummer comparison on the six fibres in the three previously pinned pairs.
hypothesis: The known high-gain quotient directions open local squareclass directions at these small bad primes that the marked generic subgroup does not already span.
primary_endpoint: At each prime, dimension of the generic-plus-selected-exceptional local image minus dimension of the generic local image.
secondary_endpoint: The same dimension difference in the product of the five local squareclass spaces, with a common generic combination required across primes.
local_model: Clear denominators by an elliptic scaling x -> d^2*x, y -> d^3*y. Use an order certified maximal at exactly the five listed primes, and exact prime-ideal valuation and residue-square characters.
reduction: Classify all thirty curve-prime cases by local minimal reduction. A denominator or a nonminimal discriminant does not by itself define bad reduction.
completeness: For odd p, dim E(Q_p)/2E(Q_p) equals the number of cubic local factors minus one. If the generic image reaches it, all rational point classes are locally covered.
bounds: Six sequential curve workers, each with a 30-second wall timeout; thirty local cases. Checkpoint each completed curve separately. No BNF, global discriminant factorization, global unit computation, new rational point, or parameter sweep.
failure_semantics: Timeouts and incomplete arithmetic remain UNKNOWN. A zero quotient support on this dictionary excludes neither other primes nor global Selmer directions.
oracle_policy: Exceptional points are labelled retrospective diagnostics only. They are not supplied to a prospective selector.
non_interference: Import the existing LocalSquareclasses implementation without a cache adapter. Never write its shared arithmetic store or any active search output.
